A character importer for your Foundry table

Ugmul’s Character
Workshop

v0.2.0 · BetaFoundry VTT 14D&D5e 6.0.6+

From D&D Beyond
to your table.

Bring a public character into Foundry without rebuilding every choice by hand. Character Workshop reads the export and builds a new actor using the approved, accessible compendium content already in your world.

It is designed to complement Ugmul’s 5.5e Automation and can also be used independently. Use the import to get started, resolve missing matches, and review the finished sheet before play.

Explore the importerInstall v0.2.0 Beta
A guided import

Your character’s choices.
Your world’s sources.

Build from existing content, resolve the gaps, and keep the result easy to review.

I.Public character import

Start with your character.
Keep the choices you made.

Enter a public D&D Beyond character number or character-service URL. The workshop reads the export and finds matching content in your world’s selected sources. A saved JSON file or pasted export works too.

No D&D Beyond login, Cloudflare account, or personal token is required.

Read the guide →

II.Your compendium sources

Use the books
already in your world.

Classes, subclasses, species, backgrounds, feats, equipment, and spells come from existing Foundry compendium documents. Their native activities, effects, and advancements stay with them.

Revised-rule classes and subclasses take priority. Legacy and Tasha’s sources remain available as fallbacks, without converting their rules.

Read the guide →

III.Resolve missing matches

Find an alternative.
Leave room for GM review.

Names and options don’t always line up across sources. Search for alternatives or open the compendium picker to choose a compatible replacement before creating the actor.

If you leave an entry at Skip, it may become a name-only placeholder with the description Needs GM Review. The GM can create, replace, or modify it afterward.

Read the guide →

IV.Native character building

Follow the build.
Finish the choices that matter.

Supported recorded choices fill Foundry’s native advancements. Remaining choices use the familiar prompts. Equipment, spells, preparation states, and proficiencies are handled as part of the import.

Canceling a prompt pauses the draft. Keep the workshop window open and use Continue Character to resume.

Read the guide →

V.Portraits and final comparison

Open the sheet.
See what needs attention.

Character artwork is saved to a local Foundry file when upload permission allows. A final comparison checks ability scores, proficiencies, expertise, and tools against the export.

The review log shows corrections, unresolved entries, and differences to check before play. Portrait cropping and token framing can be handled afterward with a tool such as Tokenizer.

Read the guide →

Current state · Beta

A starting point.
A character worth reviewing.

v0.2.0 is a beta, one-time importer. Review the completed sheet and import log before play. Unusual options, source differences, and ambiguous choices can still need manual attention.

The importer does not implement new gameplay automation for features, skills, or weapons. It includes no built-in macros or automation for unknown D&D Beyond content. Existing source activities and effects are preserved; missing mechanics are not generated from exported descriptions.

Needs GM Review entries are placeholders, not working implementations of missing features. This release creates new actors; it does not update or synchronize an existing character.

Read the beta release notes →

Before you install

Your sources.
Your permissions.

Requires Foundry VTT v14, D&D5e 6.0.6 or later, and access to compendiums containing the content you want to use. Source books are separate purchases and are not included.

The importing user needs permission to create actors and view the relevant compendiums. Local portrait saving also requires file upload permission. No automation-module dependency is required to use Character Workshop.
